```{r setup, include=FALSE}
ready <- rlang::is_installed(c("vitals", "ellmer", "digest", "jsonlite"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = ready)
library(scans)
```

You changed a prompt, a tool, or a model, and ran your evaluation again. This
article compares the two runs case by case: which outcomes changed, which
diagnostic patterns appeared or went away, and what the change cost.

vitals runs and scores the evaluation. scans reads the two completed records
and reports the recorded differences. It does not run a solver, a scorer, or
a model.

## Two runs of the same reviewed cases

The installed recipe builds everything offline. It reviews four trajectories
of the bundled investigation, turns them into versioned application examples
with `review_examples()` (one development case, three held-out cases), and
runs a baseline and a candidate version of the application through vitals
with one scorer. Every model reply is a fixed transcript, so the numbers
below show the workflow, not a real improvement.

```{r build}
source(system.file("examples", "matched-comparison.R", package = "scans"))
runs <- build_matched_comparison()
runs$baseline$manifest[c("application", "snapshot_id")]
runs$candidate$manifest[c("application", "snapshot_id")]
```

Each side is a saved investigation. That gives the comparison a snapshot
identity to cite and the frozen scanner assessments and resource measures it
compares.

`review_dataset()` used each review case identifier as the vitals sample
`id`, so the recorded `sample_id` leads back to the review:

```{r provenance}
provenance <- attr(runs$held_out, "scans_provenance")
provenance[c("group", "split", "expected_behavior")]
```

## Restrict both runs to held-out cases

Both runs also covered the development case. A change that was tuned on the
development case must be judged on cases it never saw, so keep only the
held-out samples on each side. Selecting trajectories creates a new snapshot
that records the omission.

```{r held-out}
held_out_only <- function(investigation) {
  info <- trajectory_info(investigation$bundle)
  investigation_snapshot(
    investigation$bundle,
    trajectory_ids = info$trajectory_id[info$sample_id %in% runs$held_out$id],
    application = investigation$manifest$application
  )
}
baseline <- held_out_only(runs$baseline)
candidate <- held_out_only(runs$candidate)
```

The candidate run also contained a smoke-test sample that is not in the
dataset. It is not a held-out case, so this selection leaves it out. Pairing
the unrestricted runs reports it as present only in the candidate:

```{r unrestricted}
unrestricted <- pair_trajectories(
  runs$baseline,
  runs$candidate,
  by = "sample_id",
  dataset_version = runs$examples$version_id
)
unrestricted$only_candidate$sample_id
```

## Pair on an explicit key

Name the key. Nothing is matched by position, and there is no default.

vitals does not record a dataset version or a scorer version, so you declare
both. The version of the example set is the dataset version. The scorer
declaration states that the label `expected_answer` means the same scorer,
at version 1, on both sides. vitals recorded that label because the recipe
passed a function named `expected_answer` as the scorer.

```{r pair}
scorer <- comparison_scorer(
  "expected_answer",
  version = "1",
  scale = "binary",
  direction = "higher",
  levels = c("I", "C")
)
pairing <- pair_trajectories(
  baseline,
  candidate,
  by = "sample_id",
  dataset_version = runs$examples$version_id,
  scorers = list(scorer)
)
pairing$pairs[c("pair_id", "baseline_trajectory_id", "candidate_trajectory_id")]
pairing$only_baseline["trajectory_id"]
nrow(pairing$only_candidate)
```

The candidate run stopped before the last held-out case, so that case exists
only in the baseline. It is reported, and it is outside every paired number
below. `pairing$duplicates` and `pairing$missing_key` list the other ways a
trajectory can fail to pair; both are empty here.

If the samples had run for several epochs, add `"epoch"` to `by`. Without
it, repeated epochs of a sample are reported as duplicates.

## Per-case changes

```{r compare}
comparison <- compare_trajectories(pairing)
group <- function(table) {
  provenance$group[match(table$sample_id, provenance$case_id)]
}
```

Outcomes, patterns, and resources stay in three tables. They are not combined
into a score.

```{r outcomes}
outcomes <- comparison$outcomes
data.frame(
  group = group(outcomes),
  outcomes[c("baseline_value", "candidate_value", "change")]
)
```

One case improved and one regressed. The patterns table says what the
scanners saw on each side. A side that could not be assessed is
`not_comparable`; it is never read as clean.

```{r patterns}
patterns <- comparison$patterns
changed <- patterns[patterns$change != "absent", ]
data.frame(
  group = group(changed),
  changed[c("scan", "change", "baseline_status", "candidate_status")]
)
```

The regression came with a failed tool call that the baseline did not have.

```{r resources}
resources <- comparison$resources
tokens <- resources[resources$measure == "input_tokens", ]
data.frame(
  group = group(tokens),
  tokens[c(
    "baseline_value", "candidate_value", "delta",
    "baseline_coverage", "candidate_coverage",
    "baseline_includes_cached_input", "candidate_includes_cached_input"
  )]
)
```

Both changed cases used more input tokens, including the one that improved.
A delta appears only when both sides have a complete recorded value under the
same unit, source, and cache-inclusion rule. Otherwise `delta` is `NA` and
`reason` says why:

```{r unknown}
unique(resources$reason[!resources$comparable])
```

## Open both trajectories

Every row carries both trajectory identities, and pattern rows carry the
finding and event identities on each side. Use them to read the evidence:

```{r evidence}
appeared <- changed[changed$scan == "event_error", ]
events <- trajectory_events(comparison$pairing$candidate$bundle)
events[
  events$event_id %in% appeared$candidate_event_ids[[1L]],
  c("event_type", "name", "status", "text")
]
```

Or open the comparison in the review app. The overview lists what could not
be compared first, then the matched cases, with links from each case to both
trajectories and to the cited events.

```{r app, eval=FALSE}
scans_app(comparison)
```

## Link each case to its review

The sample identity is the review case identity, so each compared case joins
back to the decision, the expected behavior, and the snapshot the reviewer
looked at.

```{r review-link}
reviewed <- merge(
  comparison$outcomes[c("sample_id", "change")],
  provenance,
  by.x = "sample_id",
  by.y = "case_id"
)
reviewed[c("group", "change", "expected_behavior")]
reviewed$origin[[1L]]$snapshot_id
```

`runs$examples$cases` holds the reviewed evidence itself: the original
trajectory, its findings, and the full decision history.

## The paired summary

Printing leads with what was not compared.

```{r summary}
comparison
```

The summary counts cases by direction. It adds an exact sign test and an
interval only when each case has one pair and at least six cases changed.
Two changed cases cannot separate a change from chance, so this summary is
counts only and its `note` says so:

```{r note}
comparison$summaries$outcomes[c("n", "n_improved", "n_regressed", "method", "note")]
```

If no case had paired, for example because the two runs used different
dataset versions, the summaries would describe each side separately, labelled
`unpaired`, with no paired estimate.

## What this establishes

- For each held-out case that both runs completed, the recorded outcome,
  findings, and resource values of the two runs, and how they differ.
- That the outcomes were compared under one scorer, at the version you
  declared, on one dataset version.
- Which cases are outside the comparison, and why.

## What it does not establish

**That the change caused the difference.** Each case ran once per side. A
model that gives different answers on repeated runs can produce the same
table with no change at all. Run several epochs to see that variation.

**Anything about a re-scored run.** Scoring the same saved outputs again with
a new scorer tests the scorer. scans reports those outcomes as incompatible,
because the scorer version differs:

```{r rescored}
rescored <- pair_trajectories(
  baseline,
  candidate,
  by = "sample_id",
  dataset_version = runs$examples$version_id,
  scorers = list(
    baseline = list(scorer),
    candidate = list(comparison_scorer(
      "expected_answer", version = "2", scale = "binary", levels = c("I", "C")
    ))
  )
)
unique(rescored$outcome_pairs[c("compatibility", "reason")])
```

To test an application or prompt change, generate new outputs for the same
cases and score both runs with the same scorer version.

**Performance on cases you tuned against.** Use the development split to
change the application and the held-out split to judge it. Once you adjust
the application in response to held-out results, those cases are no longer
held out; review new cases and make a new version of the example set.

**Complete resource use.** Coverage describes the loaded records. A complete
measure does not prove the source captured every call.

**A property of production traffic.** Three reviewed cases describe three
reviewed cases.
